 OHSAA regional championships are here with 3 key matchups
 BY 
 Ryan Johnston
 Ohio 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 AM ET Nov. 20, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 AM EST Nov. 20, 2026 
 SHARE 
 OHIO — The OHSAA football playoff field has reached the regional championships, with several battles on the gridiron on tap.
 Southwest Ohio 
 No. 2 seed Elder and No. 1 seed Princeton will battle in the Division I, Region 4 Championship at Paycor Stadium.
 The Vikings (12-0) defeated Archbishop Moeller 40-36 in their last matchup, while the Panthers (10-2) came out victorious 27-23 against St. Xavier.
 For Elder, Kaden Estep is set to use his legs and his arm to impact this game. Last game, he broke the school's all-time career total yards record, reaching 9,454 total yards.
 On the other side, Monsanna Torbert Jr. will look to lock Watson III down. He's a part of a defense that allows just 11.1 points per game. He will also have an impact on the offensive side with raw athletic speed and jumping ability.
 To watch this game live, click here .
 Central Ohio 
 No. 3 seed Massillon and No. 1 seed Watterson will battle for the Division II, Region 7 championship at Zanesville High School Stadium.
 The Tigers (10-1) are coming off a dominant 21-0 victory over Big Walnut, while the Eagles (11-0) also won a 45-12 blowout against New Albany.
 Watterson's star DE/TE Michael Boyle will look to lead the team in the trenches and in the air. His wrestling background helps him in the trenches and gives him a relentless motor.
 On the other side, Savior Owens will look to win the game on the ground. He has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards for the second straight season while averaging 7 yards per carry.
 To watch this game live, click here .
 Northern Ohio 
 No. 1 seed St. Edward and No. 3 seed Mentor are facing off in the Division I, Region 1 Championship at Parma Byers Field.
 The Eagles (11-1) are coming into this matchup riding a 38-14 victory over Hudson, while the Cardinals (10-2) won a close game against Canton McKinley 16-13.
 St. Edward will focus on pounding the rock in this matchup with Ronnie Neal Jr. The junior scored three touchdowns and was a key contributor to the win over Hudson.
 Braylon Callahan will be the head of Mentor's offensive attack going into this game. This year, the junior has scored a team-high 14 touchdowns on the ground and averages 9.3 yards per carry.
 To watch this game live, click here .
